title: When the Safehouse Burns
premise: Paloma Winterbourne, a burned-out interpreter for a collapsed peace delegation, has spent two years hiding in a government safe house after witnessing an assassination his handlers refuse to acknowledge. When the property appears on a real estate site with interior photos — including one showing him asleep on the couch — he realizes someone inside the intelligence apparatus is selling him out. Racing across three borders with a stolen decryption drive containing proof that the 'incident' was orchestrated by the delegation's own security chief, Paloma must decide whether to trust Nadia Reyes, the assassin sent to silence him but who has her own reasons to want the truth public. In the end, Paloma trades the drive for testimony at a tribunal in The Hague, exposing the conspiracy at the cost of his anonymity and any chance of ever belonging to the world he protected.
about_author: Quentin Crane is the pen name of a former diplomatic translator who spent a decade embedded with international delegations before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers drawn from the moral gray zones of back-channel diplomacy, where the truth is often the first casualty of peace.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Scrolling real estate listings at 3 a.m., Paloma finds his safe house for sale — and spots himself in a photo, identifiable by the scar on his sleeping hand. His handler dismisses his panic as paranoia, then goes silent. Emotional beat: the fragile illusion of safety shatters; Paloma realizes invisibility was always someone else's decision, not his own.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, shifting briefly to Nadia's. Fleeing to Vienna, Paloma decrypts the drive he stole during the delegation's collapse and learns the assassination was ordered by Security Chief Aldous Vane to protect arms contracts. Meanwhile, assassin Nadia Reyes tracks him — but hesitates when she recognizes Vane's signature tradecraft from a job that destroyed her family. Emotional beat: dread curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Assassin Wants
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Paloma and Nadia. Cornered in a Trieste safe flat, Paloma offers Nadia the drive instead of running; she reveals Vane burned her brother as collateral years ago. They form an uneasy alliance to deliver evidence to a Hague prosecutor before Vane's people trigger a jurisdictional blackout. Betrayed by a contact, they barely escape as their hideout burns. Emotional beat: trust kindled in the fire of mutual damage.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the tribunal, Vane's lawyers paint Paloma as unstable; the drive alone isn't enough until Nadia surrenders herself and testifies, sacrificing her freedom to corroborate him. Vane falls, but Paloma's cover identity dies with him — no more safe houses, no more invisibility. Walking out into daylight, unnamed and exposed, he finally sleeps through the night. Emotional beat: costly truth triumphs over comfortable lies; belonging found in exposure.
